Under the US Advanced Battery Consortium standard, an EV battery reaches the end of its usable life[1] when its current cell capacity is less than[2] 80%[3] of the rated capacity.

End-of-life EV batteries can be reused or repurposed, recycled, or disposed of in landfills (the landfill option would cause serious environmental issues). In the repurposing pathway, the batteries are reconfigured for a second life in applications such as grid energy storage and behind-the-meter energy storage.[4]

Regardless of whether batteries are reused, the review says they will all eventually need to be recycled.[5]
